questions.prompt: An investment bank's trading desk buys ₹200 crore of corporate bonds to hold in inventory. Which side is the bank on for that trade?
choices: Sell-side — the label describes its role as manufacturer and distributor, not the direction of a trade
Neither; proprietary trades sit outside the classification
It switches to buy-side for as long as it holds the position
questions.explanation: Sell-side. The label describes the firm's role in the system — creating, distributing and making markets in securities — not which way any individual trade went.

questions.prompt: A company needs a bank that can commit $8bn of financing on the day it signs a deal. Which type of firm can do that?
choices: An independent advisory boutique, since it has no conflicts
A sector boutique with deep industry knowledge
A bulge bracket bank, because it has the balance sheet to lend
Any of them — committed financing is arranged by the client's own lenders
questions.explanation: A bulge bracket. Independent boutiques deliberately have no balance sheet — that absence is their pitch — so they cannot underwrite or commit financing.

questions.prompt: A bank's pitch claims it is 'the number one adviser in Indian mid-market healthcare M&A by deal count'. What should you check first?
choices: Whether the ranking was audited by the exchange
The qualifiers — country, sector, size band and metric are where the ranking was won
Whether the bank is bulge bracket or boutique
The bank's own share price over the same period
questions.explanation: The qualifiers. League tables can be sliced until a firm leads one, and deal count measures volume rather than how well the clients did.

questions.prompt: Buy-side firms typically earn a percentage of assets under management annually, whether or not markets rise.
questions.explanation: True. Buy-side revenue is largely a recurring fee on assets, sometimes with a performance fee on top — unlike sell-side revenue, which is transactional and close to zero in a quiet quarter.

questions.prompt: A founder is choosing between a bulge bracket bank and an independent advisory boutique to sell her company. Set out the real trade-off, and explain what each firm's fee model means for the advice she will receive.
rubric: Identifies that the bulge bracket brings a balance sheet, underwriting and distribution reach the boutique does not have
Identifies the boutique's pitch as fewer conflicts, because it has no securities to sell and no lending relationship to protect
Notes that sell-side advisory fees are largely contingent on completion, giving both firms a structural interest in a deal happening
Draws the consequence: advice to transact should be weighed knowing the adviser is paid mainly if she transacts
Reaches a reasoned position rather than declaring one option universally better — e.g. deal size, financing need, and sector depth decide it
